title: Hybridization Orbital Mixing Diagram
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: AP Chemistry
description: Interactive diagram with three panels for sp, sp2, and sp3 hybridization. Each panel shows the 2s and 2p orbitals before mixing, the hybrid and leftover p orbitals after mixing, and the resulting geometry and bond angle. A practice mode asks for the hybridization of the central atom in eight common molecules.

learningObjectives: Explain how atomic orbitals combine to form hybrid orbitals
Connect hybridization type to electron geometry and bond angle
Determine the hybridization of a central atom from the number of electron groups
standards: AP Chemistry CED Unit 2, Topic 2.7: VSEPR and Hybridization

controls.label: Mode
controls.description: Explore mode, or a practice question for one of eight molecules

controls.label: Panels
controls.description: Click a panel to see its details (Explore) or to answer the practice question

equations: number of hybrid orbitals = number of atomic orbitals mixed
electron groups = bonded atoms + lone pairs
assumptions: Only sp, sp2, and sp3 hybridization are shown, matching the chapter
Box height indicates relative energy only; it is not to scale
The geometry pictures are two-dimensional sketches of the hybrid orbital directions

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Click-to-reveal comparison followed by practice questions with feedback
keyQuestions: Why are there always four orbital boxes before and after mixing?
What are the leftover p orbitals used for?
Why do methane, ammonia, and water share the same hybridization but have different shapes?
commonMisconceptions: Counting a double bond as two electron groups
Thinking hybridization is a physical event rather than a model
Assuming lone pairs do not occupy hybrid orbitals
assessmentOpportunities: Eight built-in practice questions with immediate feedback
